# tokio - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tokio/^1/

## Expand description

A runtime for writing reliable network applications without compromising speed.

Tokio is an event-driven, non-blocking I/O platform for writing asynchronous applications with the Rust programming language. At a high level, it provides a few major components:

- Tools for [working with asynchronous tasks](https://docs.rs#working-with-tasks), including[synchronization primitives and channels](https://docs.rs/sync/index.html)and[timeouts, sleeps, and intervals](https://docs.rs/time/index.html).
- APIs for [performing asynchronous I/O](https://docs.rs#asynchronous-io), including[TCP and UDP](https://docs.rs/net/index.html)sockets,[filesystem](https://docs.rs/fs/index.html)operations, and[process](https://docs.rs/process/index.html)and[signal](https://docs.rs/signal/index.html)management.
- A [runtime](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)for executing asynchronous code, including a task scheduler, an I/O driver backed by the operating system’s event queue (`epoll`,`kqueue`,`IOCP`, etc…), and a high performance timer.

Guide level documentation is found on the [website](https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial).

[§](https://docs.rs#a-tour-of-tokio)A Tour of Tokio

Tokio consists of a number of modules that provide a range of functionality essential for implementing asynchronous applications in Rust. In this section, we will take a brief tour of Tokio, summarizing the major APIs and their uses.

The easiest way to get started is to enable all features. Do this by
enabling the `full` feature flag:

`tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#authoring-applications)Authoring applications

Tokio is great for writing applications and most users in this case shouldn’t
worry too much about what features they should pick. If you’re unsure, we suggest
going with `full` to ensure that you don’t run into any road blocks while you’re
building your application.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

This example shows the quickest way to get started with Tokio.

`tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#authoring-libraries)Authoring libraries

As a library author your goal should be to provide the lightest weight crate that is based on Tokio. To achieve this you should ensure that you only enable the features you need. This allows users to pick up your crate without having to enable unnecessary features.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

This example shows how you may want to import features for a library that just
needs to `tokio::spawn` and use a `TcpStream`.

`tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt", "net"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#working-with-tasks)Working With Tasks

Asynchronous programs in Rust are based around lightweight, non-blocking
units of execution called [ tasks](https://docs.rs#working-with-tasks). The

[module provides important tools for working with tasks:](https://docs.rs/task/index.html)

`tokio::task`- The `spawn``JoinHandle`
- Functions for [running blocking operations](https://docs.rs/task/index.html#blocking-and-yielding)in an asynchronous task context.

The [ tokio::task](https://docs.rs/task/index.html) module is present only when the “rt” feature flag
is enabled.

The [ tokio::sync](https://docs.rs/sync/index.html) module contains synchronization primitives to use when
needing to communicate or share data. These include:

- channels (`oneshot``mpsc``watch``broadcast`
- a non-blocking `Mutex`
- an asynchronous `Barrier`

The `tokio::sync` module is present only when the “sync” feature flag is
enabled.

The [ tokio::time](https://docs.rs/time/index.html) module provides utilities for tracking time and
scheduling work. This includes functions for setting

[timeouts](https://docs.rs/time/fn.timeout.html)for tasks,

[sleeping](https://docs.rs/time/fn.sleep.html)work to run in the future, or

[repeating an operation at an interval](https://docs.rs/time/fn.interval.html).

In order to use `tokio::time`, the “time” feature flag must be enabled.

Finally, Tokio provides a *runtime* for executing asynchronous tasks. Most
applications can use the [ #[tokio::main]](https://docs.rs/attr.main.html) macro to run their code on the
Tokio runtime. However, this macro provides only basic configuration options. As
an alternative, the

[module provides more powerful APIs for configuring and managing runtimes. You should use that module if the](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)

`tokio::runtime``#[tokio::main]` macro doesn’t
provide the functionality you need.Using the runtime requires the “rt” or “rt-multi-thread” feature flags, to
enable the current-thread [single-threaded scheduler](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html#current-thread-scheduler) and the [multi-thread
scheduler](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html#multi-thread-scheduler), respectively. See the [ runtime module
documentation](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html#runtime-scheduler) for details. In addition, the “macros” feature
flag enables the

`#[tokio::main]` and `#[tokio::test]` attributes.[§](https://docs.rs#cpu-bound-tasks-and-blocking-code)CPU-bound tasks and blocking code

Tokio is able to concurrently run many tasks on a few threads by repeatedly
swapping the currently running task on each thread. However, this kind of
swapping can only happen at `.await` points, so code that spends a long time
without reaching an `.await` will prevent other tasks from running. To
combat this, Tokio provides two kinds of threads: Core threads and blocking threads.

The core threads are where all asynchronous code runs, and Tokio will by default
spawn one for each CPU core. You can use the environment variable `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS`
to override the default value.

The blocking threads are spawned on demand, can be used to run blocking code
that would otherwise block other tasks from running and are kept alive when
not used for a certain amount of time which can be configured with [ thread_keep_alive](https://docs.rs/runtime/struct.Builder.html#method.thread_keep_alive).
Since it is not possible for Tokio to swap out blocking tasks, like it
can do with asynchronous code, the upper limit on the number of blocking
threads is very large. These limits can be configured on the

[.](https://docs.rs/runtime/struct.Builder.html)

`Builder`To spawn a blocking task, you should use the [ spawn_blocking](https://docs.rs/task/fn.spawn_blocking.html) function.

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    // This is running on a core thread.
    let blocking_task = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(|| {
        // This is running on a blocking thread.
        // Blocking here is ok.
    });
    // We can wait for the blocking task like this:
    // If the blocking task panics, the unwrap below will propagate the
    // panic.
    blocking_task.await.unwrap();
}
```
If your code is CPU-bound and you wish to limit the number of threads used
to run it, you should use a separate thread pool dedicated to CPU bound tasks.
For example, you could consider using the [rayon](https://docs.rs/rayon) library for CPU-bound
tasks. It is also possible to create an extra Tokio runtime dedicated to
CPU-bound tasks, but if you do this, you should be careful that the extra
runtime runs *only* CPU-bound tasks, as IO-bound tasks on that runtime
will behave poorly.

Hint: If using rayon, you can use a [ oneshot](https://docs.rs/sync/oneshot/index.html) channel to send the result back
to Tokio when the rayon task finishes.

[§](https://docs.rs#asynchronous-io)Asynchronous IO

As well as scheduling and running tasks, Tokio provides everything you need to perform input and output asynchronously.

The [ tokio::io](https://docs.rs/io/index.html) module provides Tokio’s asynchronous core I/O primitives,
the

[,](https://docs.rs/io/trait.AsyncRead.html)

`AsyncRead`[, and](https://docs.rs/io/trait.AsyncWrite.html)

`AsyncWrite`[traits. In addition, when the “io-util” feature flag is enabled, it also provides combinators and functions for working with these traits, forming as an asynchronous counterpart to](https://docs.rs/io/trait.AsyncBufRead.html)

`AsyncBufRead`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html)

`std::io`Tokio also includes APIs for performing various kinds of I/O and interacting with the operating system asynchronously. These include:

- `tokio::net`- [TCP](https://docs.rs/net/tcp/index.html),- [UDP](https://docs.rs/net/struct.UdpSocket.html), and- [Unix Domain Sockets](https://docs.rs/net/unix/index.html)(enabled by the “net” feature flag),
- `tokio::fs`- `std::fs`
- `tokio::signal`
- `tokio::process`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

A simple TCP echo server:

```
use tokio::net::TcpListener;
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:8080").await?;
    loop {
        let (mut socket, _) = listener.accept().await?;
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut buf = [0; 1024];
            // In a loop, read data from the socket and write the data back.
            loop {
                let n = match socket.read(&mut buf).await {
                    // socket closed
                    Ok(0) => return,
                    Ok(n) => n,
                    Err(e) => {
                        eprintln!("failed to read from socket; err = {:?}", e);
                        return;
                    }
                };
                // Write the data back
                if let Err(e) = socket.write_all(&buf[0..n]).await {
                    eprintln!("failed to write to socket; err = {:?}", e);
                    return;
                }
            }
        });
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

Tokio uses a set of [feature flags](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-features-section) to reduce the amount of compiled code. It
is possible to just enable certain features over others. By default, Tokio
does not enable any features but allows one to enable a subset for their use
case. Below is a list of the available feature flags. You may also notice
above each function, struct and trait there is listed one or more feature flags
that are required for that item to be used. If you are new to Tokio it is
recommended that you use the `full` feature flag which will enable all public APIs.
Beware though that this will pull in many extra dependencies that you may not
need.

- `full`: Enables all features listed below except- `test-util`and unstable features.
- `rt`: Enables- `tokio::spawn`, the current-thread scheduler, and non-scheduler utilities.
- `rt-multi-thread`: Enables the heavier, multi-threaded, work-stealing scheduler.
- `io-util`: Enables the IO based- `Ext`traits.
- `io-std`: Enable- `Stdout`,- `Stdin`and- `Stderr`types.
- `net`: Enables- `tokio::net`types such as- `TcpStream`,- `UnixStream`and- `UdpSocket`, as well as (on Unix-like systems)- `AsyncFd`and (on FreeBSD)- `PollAio`.
- `time`: Enables- `tokio::time`types and allows the schedulers to enable the built-in timer.
- `process`: Enables- `tokio::process`types.
- `macros`: Enables- `#[tokio::main]`and- `#[tokio::test]`macros.
- `sync`: Enables all- `tokio::sync`types.
- `signal`: Enables all- `tokio::signal`types.
- `fs`: Enables- `tokio::fs`types.
- `test-util`: Enables testing based infrastructure for the Tokio runtime.
- `parking_lot`: As a potential optimization, use the- `parking_lot`- `const`context.- `MSRV`may increase according to the- `parking_lot`

*Note:  AsyncRead and AsyncWrite traits do not require any features and are
always available.*

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

Some feature flags are only available when specifying the `tokio_unstable` flag:

- `tracing`: Enables tracing events.
- `io-uring`: Enables- `io-uring`(Linux only).
- `taskdump`: Enables- `taskdump`(Linux only).

Likewise, this flag enables access to unstable APIs.

This flag enables **unstable** features. The public API of these features
may break in 1.x releases. To enable these features, the `--cfg tokio_unstable` argument must be passed to `rustc` when compiling. This
serves to explicitly opt-in to features which may break semver conventions,
since Cargo [does not yet directly support such opt-ins](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/feature-request-unstable-opt-in-non-transitive-crate-features/16193#why-not-a-crate-feature-2).

You can specify it in your project’s `.cargo/config.toml` file:

```
[build]
rustflags = ["--cfg", "tokio_unstable"]
```
`[build]` section does **not**go in a

`Cargo.toml` file. Instead it must be placed in the Cargo config
file `.cargo/config.toml`.
Alternatively, you can specify it with an environment variable:

```
## Many *nix shells:
export RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable"
cargo build
```
```
## Windows PowerShell:
$Env:RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable"
cargo build
```
[§](https://docs.rs#supported-platforms)Supported platforms

Tokio currently guarantees support for the following platforms:

- Linux
- Windows
- Android (API level 21)
- macOS
- iOS
- FreeBSD

Tokio will continue to support these platforms in the future. However, future releases may change requirements such as the minimum required libc version on Linux, the API level on Android, or the supported FreeBSD release.

Beyond the above platforms, Tokio is intended to work on all platforms
supported by the mio crate. You can find a longer list [in mio’s
documentation](https://crates.io/crates/mio#platforms). However, these additional platforms may
become unsupported in the future.

Note that Wine is considered to be a different platform from Windows. See mio’s documentation for more information on Wine support.

[§](https://docs.rs#wasm-support)`WASM` support

Tokio has some limited support for the `WASM` platform. Without the
`tokio_unstable` flag, the following features are supported:

- `sync`
- `macros`
- `io-util`
- `rt`
- `time`

Enabling any other feature (including `full`) will cause a compilation
failure.

The `time` module will only work on `WASM` platforms that have support for
timers (e.g. wasm32-wasi). The timing functions will panic if used on a `WASM`
platform that does not support timers.

Note also that if the runtime becomes indefinitely idle, it will panic immediately instead of blocking forever. On platforms that don’t support time, this means that the runtime can never be idle in any way.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-wasm-support)Unstable `WASM` support

Tokio also has unstable support for some additional `WASM` features. This
requires the use of the `tokio_unstable` flag.

Using this flag enables the use of `tokio::net` on the wasm32-wasi target.
However, not all methods are available on the networking types as `WASI`
currently does not support the creation of new sockets from within `WASM`.
Because of this, sockets must currently be created via the `FromRawFd`
trait.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use task::`- [spawn](https://docs.rs/task/fn.spawn.html);- `rt`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [doc](https://docs.rs/doc/index.html)- `docsrs`and Unix
- Types which are documented locally in the Tokio crate, but does not actually live here.
- [fs](https://docs.rs/fs/index.html)- `fs`
- Asynchronous file utilities.
- [io](https://docs.rs/io/index.html)
- Traits, helpers, and type definitions for asynchronous I/O functionality.
- [net](https://docs.rs/net/index.html)
- TCP/UDP/Unix bindings for `tokio`.
- [process](https://docs.rs/process/index.html)- `process`
- An implementation of asynchronous process management for Tokio.
- [runtime](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)- `rt`
- The Tokio runtime.
- [signal](https://docs.rs/signal/index.html)- `signal`
- Asynchronous signal handling for Tokio.
- [stream](https://docs.rs/stream/index.html)
- Due to the `Stream`trait’s inclusion in`std`landing later than Tokio’s 1.0 release, most of the Tokio stream utilities have been moved into the`tokio-stream`
- [sync](https://docs.rs/sync/index.html)- `sync`
- Synchronization primitives for use in asynchronous contexts.
- [task](https://docs.rs/task/index.html)- `rt`
- Asynchronous green-threads.
- [time](https://docs.rs/time/index.html)- `time`
- Utilities for tracking time.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [join](https://docs.rs/macro.join.html)- `macros`
- Waits on multiple concurrent branches, returning when **all**branches complete.
- [pin](https://docs.rs/macro.pin.html)
- Pins a value on the stack.
- [select](https://docs.rs/macro.select.html)- `macros`
- Waits on multiple concurrent branches, returning when the **first**branch completes, cancelling the remaining branches.
- [task_](https://docs.rs/macro.task_local.html)- local - `rt`
- Declares a new task-local key of type `tokio::task::LocalKey`
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_join.html)- join - `macros`
- Waits on multiple concurrent branches, returning when **all**branches complete with`Ok(_)`or on the first`Err(_)`.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [main](https://docs.rs/attr.main.html)- `rt`and- `macros`
- Marks async function to be executed by the selected runtime. This macro
helps set up a `Runtime`without requiring the user to use[Runtime](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Runtime.html)or[Builder](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Builder.html)directly.
- [test](https://docs.rs/attr.test.html)- `rt`and- `macros`
- Marks async function to be executed by runtime, suitable to test environment.
This macro helps set up a `Runtime`without requiring the user to use[Runtime](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Runtime.html)or[Builder](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Builder.html)directly.

[64](#64)pub async fn serve_stdio(repo: PathBuf, config: OkConfig) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
[65](#65)    let store_path = repo.join(".ok/index.sqlite");
[66](#66)    let mut store = SqliteStore::open(&store_path)?;
[67](#67)    let mut last_request = Instant::now();
[68](#68)    let stdin = BufReader::new(tokio::io::stdin());
[69](#69)    let mut lines = stdin.lines();
[70](#70)    let mut stdout = tokio::io::stdout();
[71](#71)    while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await? {
[72](#72)        if line.trim().is_empty() {
[73](#73)            continue;
[74](#74)        }
[75](#75)        if store_idle_expired(last_request) {
[76](#76)            store = SqliteStore::open(&store_path)?;
[77](#77)        }
[78](#78)        last_request = Instant::now();
[79](#79)        let response = handle_line(&repo, &store, &config, &line).await;
[80](#80)        stdout
[81](#81)            .write_all(format!("{}\n", serde_json::to_string(&response)?).as_bytes())
[82](#82)            .await?;
[83](#83)        stdout.flush().await?;
[84](#84)    }
[85](#85)    Ok(())
[86](#86)}
[87](#87)
[88](#88)async fn handle_line(
[89](#89)    repo: &Path,
[90](#90)    store: &SqliteStore,
[91](#91)    config: &OkConfig,
[92](#92)    line: &str,
[93](#93)) -> JsonRpcResponse {
[94](#94)    match serde_json::from_str::<JsonRpcRequest>(line) {
[95](#95)        Ok(request) => handle_request(repo, store, config, request).await,
[96](#96)        Err(err) => JsonRpcResponse {
[97](#97)            jsonrpc: "2.0",
[98](#98)            id: None,
[99](#99)            result: None,
[100](#100)            error: Some(json!({"code": -32700, "message": err.to_string()})),
[101](#101)        },
[102](#102)    }
[103](#103)}

[114](#114)async fn handle_request_with_timeout(
[115](#115)    repo: &Path,
[116](#116)    store: &SqliteStore,
[117](#117)    config: &OkConfig,
[118](#118)    request: JsonRpcRequest,
[119](#119)    timeout: Duration,
[120](#120)) -> JsonRpcResponse {
[121](#121)    let id = request.id.clone();
[122](#122)    let Some(method) = request.method.as_deref() else {
[123](#123)        return JsonRpcResponse {
[124](#124)            jsonrpc: "2.0",
[125](#125)            id,
[126](#126)            result: None,
[127](#127)            error: Some(json!({"code": -32600, "message": "missing required JSON-RPC method"})),
[128](#128)        };
[129](#129)    };
[130](#130)    let result = tokio::time::timeout(
[131](#131)        timeout,
[132](#132)        dispatch(repo, store, config, method, request.params),
[133](#133)    )
[134](#134)    .await;
[135](#135)    match result {
[136](#136)        Ok(Ok(value)) => JsonRpcResponse {
[137](#137)            jsonrpc: "2.0",
[138](#138)            id,
[139](#139)            result: Some(value),
[140](#140)            error: None,
[141](#141)        },
[142](#142)        Ok(Err(err)) => JsonRpcResponse {
[143](#143)            jsonrpc: "2.0",
[144](#144)            id,
[145](#145)            result: None,
[146](#146)            error: Some(json!({"code": -32000, "message": err.to_string()})),
[147](#147)        },
[148](#148)        Err(_) => JsonRpcResponse {
[149](#149)            jsonrpc: "2.0",
[150](#150)            id,
[151](#151)            result: None,
[152](#152)            error: Some(
[153](#153)                json!({"code": -32001, "message": format!("MCP method `{method}` timed out after {}s", timeout.as_secs())}),
[154](#154)            ),
[155](#155)        },
[156](#156)    }

[159](#159)fn store_idle_expired(last_request: Instant) -> bool {
[160](#160)    last_request.elapsed() > STORE_IDLE_TTL
[161](#161)}

[163](#163)async fn dispatch(
[164](#164)    repo: &Path,
[165](#165)    store: &SqliteStore,
[166](#166)    config: &OkConfig,
[167](#167)    method: &str,
[168](#168)    params: Value,
[169](#169)) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
[170](#170)    let gate = PolicyGate::new(config);
[171](#171)    match method {
[172](#172)        "initialize" => {
[173](#173)            let client_version = params
[174](#174)                .get("protocolVersion")
[175](#175)                .and_then(Value::as_str)
[176](#176)                .unwrap_or("2024-11-05");
[177](#177)            Ok(json!({
[178](#178)                "protocolVersion": client_version,
[179](#179)                "serverInfo": {"name": "open-kioku", "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")},
[180](#180)                "capabilities": {"tools": {}}
[181](#181)            }))
[182](#182)        }
[183](#183)        "tools/list" => {
[184](#184)            let (tool_list, unstable) = tools(config);
[185](#185)            Ok(json!({
[186](#186)                "tools": tool_list,
[187](#187)                "_unstable_experimental_tools": unstable
[188](#188)            }))
[189](#189)        }
[190](#190)        "tools/call" => {
[191](#191)            let name = params
[192](#192)                .get("name")
[193](#193)                .and_then(Value::as_str)
[194](#194)                .unwrap_or_default();
[195](#195)            let args = params
[196](#196)                .get("arguments")
[197](#197)                .cloned()
[198](#198)                .unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
[199](#199)            call_tool(repo, store, config, name, args).await
[200](#200)        }
[201](#201)        #[cfg(test)]
[202](#202)        "__test_sleep" => {
[203](#203)            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
[204](#204)            Ok(json!({"slept": true}))
[205](#205)        }
[206](#206)        "repo_status" => Ok(json!(store.manifest()?)),
[207](#207)        "list_languages" => {
[208](#208)            let files = store.list_files(usize::MAX, 0)?;
[209](#209)            let mut languages = files
[210](#210)                .into_iter()
[211](#211)                .map(|file| format!("{:?}", file.language))
[212](#212)                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[213](#213)            languages.sort();
[214](#214)            languages.dedup();
[215](#215)            Ok(json!({"languages": languages}))
[216](#216)        }
[217](#217)        "list_files" => {
[218](#218)            gate.ensure_allowed(ActionKind::Read)?;
[219](#219)            let limit = limit(¶ms);
[220](#220)            let offset = offset(¶ms);
[221](#221)            Ok(paged_overfetch_response(
[222](#222)                "files",
[223](#223)                store.list_files(overfetch_limit(limit), offset)?,
[224](#224)                limit,
[225](#225)                offset,
[226](#226)            )?)
[227](#227)        }
[228](#228)        "list_symbols" | "search_symbols" => {
[229](#229)            let query = params.get("query").and_then(Value::as_str);
[230](#230)            let limit = limit(¶ms);
[231](#231)            let offset = offset(¶ms);
[232](#232)            Ok(paged_overfetch_response(

[239](#239)        "search_code" | "search_files" => search_tool(repo, store, ¶ms),
[240](#240)        "regex_search" => search_tool(repo, store, ¶ms),
[241](#241)        "build_context_pack" => {
[242](#242)            let task = required_str(¶ms, "task")?;
[243](#243)            let mut pack = ContextPackBuilder::new(store as &dyn OkStore)
[244](#244)                .with_history_store(Some(store))
[245](#245)                .build(task, limit(¶ms))?;
[246](#246)            pack.architecture_policy = configured_architecture_policy_report(repo, store)?;
[247](#247)            let format_arg = params
[248](#248)                .get("format")
[249](#249)                .and_then(Value::as_str)
[250](#250)                .unwrap_or("json");
[251](#251)            match format_arg {
[252](#252)                "markdown" => Ok(json!(
[253](#253)                    open_kioku_context::ContextPackFormat::Markdown.render(&pack)?
[254](#254)                )),

[256](#256)                _ => Ok(json!(pack)),

[259](#259)        "build_compressed_context" => {

[264](#264)            pack.architecture_policy = configured_architecture_policy_report(repo, store)?;
[265](#265)            let compressed = ContextHandleStore::open_repo(repo)?.compress_pack(&pack)?;
[266](#266)            let format_arg = params
[267](#267)                .get("format")
[268](#268)                .and_then(Value::as_str)
[269](#269)                .unwrap_or("json");
[270](#270)            if format_arg == "toon" {
[271](#271)                Ok(json!(open_kioku_format::render_compressed_context_toon(
[272](#272)                    &compressed

[274](#274)            } else {

[653](#653)        "apply_patch" => {

[664](#664)        "get_evidence_schema" => {
[665](#665)            let manifest = store.manifest().ok().flatten();

[672](#672)        "query_evidence_graph" => {
[673](#673)            let query_str = params
[674](#674)                .get("query")
[675](#675)                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
[676](#676)                .unwrap_or("");
[677](#677)            let limit = params
[678](#678)                .get("limit")
[679](#679)                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_u64)
[680](#680)                .map(|n| n as usize);
[681](#681)            let offset = params
[682](#682)                .get("offset")
[683](#683)                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_u64)
[684](#684)                .map(|n| n as usize);
[685](#685)
[686](#686)            let ast = match open_kioku_graph::query::parse_graph_query(query_str) {
[687](#687)                Ok(ast) => ast,
[688](#688)                Err(e) => {
[689](#689)                    let (kind, message) = match e {
[690](#690)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::ParseError(m) => {
[691](#691)                            ("parse_error", m)
[692](#692)                        }
[693](#693)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::QueryRejected(m) => {
[694](#694)                            ("query_rejected", m)
[695](#695)                        }
[696](#696)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnknownNodeType(m) => {
[697](#697)                            ("unknown_node_type", m)
[698](#698)                        }
[699](#699)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnknownEdgeType(m) => {
[700](#700)                            ("unknown_edge_type", m)
[701](#701)                        }
[702](#702)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnsupportedFilter(m) => {
[703](#703)                            ("unsupported_filter", m.clone())
[704](#704)                        }
[705](#705)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::DepthLimitExceeded(requested) => {
[706](#706)                            (
[707](#707)                                "depth_limit_exceeded",
[708](#708)                                format!("requested {} exceeds limit", requested),
[709](#709)                            )
[710](#710)                        }
[711](#711)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::LimitExceeded(requested) => (
[712](#712)                            "limit_exceeded",
[713](#713)                            format!("requested {} exceeds limit", requested),
[714](#714)                        ),
[715](#715)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnboundVariable(m) => {
[716](#716)                            ("unbound_variable", m.clone())
[717](#717)                        }
[718](#718)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::Timeout => {
[719](#719)                            ("timeout", "Query execution timed out".to_string())
[720](#720)                        }
[721](#721)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::Storage(e) => {
[722](#722)                            ("storage_error", e.to_string())
[723](#723)                        }
[724](#724)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::Serde(e) => {
[725](#725)                            ("serde_error", e.to_string())
[726](#726)                        }
[727](#727)                    };
[728](#728)                    return Ok(serde_json::json!({
[729](#729)                        "error": {
[730](#730)                            "kind": kind,
[731](#731)                            "message": message,
[732](#732)                        }
[733](#733)                    }));
[734](#734)                }
[735](#735)            };
[736](#736)
[737](#737)            let mut options = open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryOptions::default();
[738](#738)            if let Some(l) = limit {
[739](#739)                options.limit = l.min(MAX_MCP_LIMIT);
[740](#740)            }
[741](#741)            if let Some(offset) = offset {
[742](#742)                options.offset = offset;
[743](#743)            }
[744](#744)
[745](#745)            match open_kioku_graph::query::execute_graph_query(
[746](#746)                store as &dyn open_kioku_storage::GraphStore,
[747](#747)                &ast,
[748](#748)                options,
[749](#749)            ) {
[750](#750)                Ok(result) => graph_query_response(query_str, ¶ms, result),
[751](#751)                Err(e) => {
[752](#752)                    let (kind, message) = match e {
[753](#753)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::ParseError(m) => {
[754](#754)                            ("parse_error", m)
[755](#755)                        }
[756](#756)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::QueryRejected(m) => {
[757](#757)                            ("query_rejected", m)
[758](#758)                        }
[759](#759)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnknownNodeType(m) => {
[760](#760)                            ("unknown_node_type", m)
[761](#761)                        }
[762](#762)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnknownEdgeType(m) => {
[763](#763)                            ("unknown_edge_type", m)
[764](#764)                        }
[765](#765)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnsupportedFilter(m) => {
[766](#766)                            ("unsupported_filter", m.clone())
[767](#767)                        }
[768](#768)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::DepthLimitExceeded(requested) => {
[769](#769)                            (
[770](#770)                                "depth_limit_exceeded",
[771](#771)                                format!("requested {} exceeds limit", requested),
[772](#772)                            )
[773](#773)                        }
[774](#774)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::LimitExceeded(requested) => (
[775](#775)                            "limit_exceeded",
[776](#776)                            format!("requested {} exceeds limit", requested),
[777](#777)                        ),
[778](#778)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::UnboundVariable(m) => {
[779](#779)                            ("unbound_variable", m.clone())
[780](#780)                        }
[781](#781)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::Timeout => {
[782](#782)                            ("timeout", "Query execution timed out".to_string())
[783](#783)                        }
[784](#784)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::Storage(e) => {
[785](#785)                            ("storage_error", e.to_string())
[786](#786)                        }
[787](#787)                        open_kioku_graph::query::GraphQueryError::Serde(e) => {
[788](#788)                            ("serde_error", e.to_string())
[789](#789)                        }
[790](#790)                    };
[791](#791)                    Ok(serde_json::json!({
[792](#792)                        "error": {
[793](#793)                            "kind": kind,
[794](#794)                            "message": message,
[795](#795)                        }
[796](#796)                    }))
[797](#797)                }
[798](#798)            }
[799](#799)        }
[800](#800)        "map_stacktrace_to_code" | "find_errors_for_symbol" | "find_recent_failures" => {
[801](#801)            Ok(json!(disabled_response(method)))
[802](#802)        }
[803](#803)        other => anyhow::bail!("unknown MCP method or tool `{other}`"),
[804](#804)    }
[805](#805)}
[806](#806)
[807](#807)fn call_tool<'a>(
[808](#808)    repo: &'a Path,
[809](#809)    store: &'a SqliteStore,
[810](#810)    config: &'a OkConfig,
[811](#811)    name: &'a str,
[812](#812)    args: Value,
[813](#813)) -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = anyhow::Result<Value>> + Send + 'a>> {
[814](#814)    Box::pin(async move {
[815](#815)        dispatch(repo, store, config, name, args)
[816](#816)            .await
[817](#817)            .map(|value| {
[818](#818)                let mut text = if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {
[819](#819)                    s.to_string()
[820](#820)                } else {
[821](#821)                    serde_json::to_string_pretty(&value).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".into())
[822](#822)                };
[823](#823)                let text_truncated = truncate_utf8(&mut text, MAX_TOOL_TEXT_BYTES);
[824](#824)                let structured_content = match value {
[825](#825)                    Value::Object(_) => value,
[826](#826)                    other => json!({ "value": other }),
[827](#827)                };
[828](#828)                let mut response = json!({
[829](#829)                    "content": [{"type": "text", "text": text}],
[830](#830)                    "structuredContent": structured_content
[831](#831)                });
[832](#832)                if text_truncated {
[833](#833)                    response["truncated"] = json!(true);
[834](#834)                    response["warnings"] = json!([format!(
[835](#835)                        "tool text content was truncated to {} bytes; structuredContent remains available",
[836](#836)                        MAX_TOOL_TEXT_BYTES
[837](#837)                    )]);
[838](#838)                }
[839](#839)                response
[840](#840)            })
[841](#841)    })
[842](#842)}
[843](#843)
[844](#844)fn search_tool(repo: &Path, store: &dyn MetadataStore, params: &Value) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
[845](#845)    let limit = limit(params);
[846](#846)    let offset = offset(params);
[847](#847)    let results = search_results(repo, store, params, search_fetch_limit(limit, offset))?;
[848](#848)    paged_bounded_slice_response("results", results, limit, offset)
[849](#849)}
[850](#850)
[851](#851)fn search_results(
[852](#852)    repo: &Path,
[853](#853)    store: &dyn MetadataStore,
[854](#854)    params: &Value,
[855](#855)    fetch_limit: usize,
[856](#856)) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<open_kioku_core::SearchResult>> {
[857](#857)    let query = params
[858](#858)        .get("query")
[859](#859)        .or_else(|| params.get("pattern"))
[860](#860)        .and_then(Value::as_str)
[861](#861)        .unwrap_or_default();
[862](#862)    let mode = params.get("mode").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("code");
[863](#863)    let index_dir = default_index_dir(repo);
[864](#864)    if TantivySearchIndex::exists(&index_dir) {
[865](#865)        let index = TantivySearchIndex::open_or_create(index_dir)?;
[866](#866)        if mode == "graph" {
[867](#867)            return Ok(index.search_graph(query, fetch_limit)?);
[868](#868)        }
[869](#869)        return Ok(index.search(query, fetch_limit)?);
[870](#870)    }
[871](#871)    if mode == "graph" {
[872](#872)        anyhow::bail!("graph search index is missing; run `ok index .` first");
[873](#873)    }
[874](#874)    let files = store.list_files(usize::MAX, 0)?;
[875](#875)    let chunks = store.all_chunks()?;
[876](#876)    let symbols = store.list_symbols(None, usize::MAX, 0)?;
[877](#877)    Ok(search_chunks(
[878](#878)        &chunks,
[879](#879)        &files,
[880](#880)        &symbols,
[881](#881)        query,
[882](#882)        fetch_limit,
[883](#883)    )?)
[884](#884)}
[885](#885)
[886](#886)fn semantic_search_tool(
[887](#887)    repo: &Path,
[888](#888)    store: &dyn MetadataStore,
[889](#889)    config: &OkConfig,
[890](#890)    params: &Value,
[891](#891)) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
[892](#892)    let query = required_str(params, "query")?;
[893](#893)    let mut semantic_config = config.semantic.clone();
[894](#894)    semantic_config.enabled = true;
[895](#895)    let manager = SemanticIndexManager::new(repo, store, &semantic_config);
[896](#896)    let status = manager.status();
[897](#897)    if status.ready {
[898](#898)        let limit = limit(params);
[899](#899)        let offset = offset(params);
[900](#900)        let results = manager.search(query, search_fetch_limit(limit, offset))?;
[901](#901)        let mut response = paged_bounded_slice_response("results", results, limit, offset)?;
[902](#902)        response["semantic_status"] = json!(status);
[903](#903)        return Ok(response);
[904](#904)    }
[905](#905)    let mut response = paged_slice_response::<open_kioku_core::SearchResult>(
[906](#906)        "results",
[907](#907)        Vec::new(),
[908](#908)        limit(params),
[909](#909)        offset(params),
[910](#910)    )?;
[911](#911)    response["semantic_status"] = json!(status);
[912](#912)    response["error"] = json!("semantic index is not ready; run `ok semantic index` first");
[913](#913)    Ok(response)
[914](#914)}
[915](#915)
[916](#916)fn semantic_status_tool(
[917](#917)    repo: &Path,
[918](#918)    store: &dyn MetadataStore,
[919](#919)    config: &OkConfig,
[920](#920)) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
[921](#921)    let manager = SemanticIndexManager::new(repo, store, &config.semantic);
[922](#922)    Ok(json!(manager.status()))
[923](#923)}
[924](#924)
[925](#925)fn hybrid_search_tool(
[926](#926)    repo: &Path,
[927](#927)    store: &dyn MetadataStore,
[928](#928)    config: &OkConfig,
[929](#929)    params: &Value,
[930](#930)) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
[931](#931)    let query = required_str(params, "query")?;
[932](#932)    let limit = limit(params);
[933](#933)    let offset = offset(params);
[934](#934)    let mut results = search_results(repo, store, params, search_fetch_limit(limit, offset))?;
[935](#935)    let mut semantic_config = config.semantic.clone();
[936](#936)    semantic_config.enabled = true;
[937](#937)    let manager = SemanticIndexManager::new(repo, store, &semantic_config);
[938](#938)    let status = manager.status();
[939](#939)    if status.ready {
[940](#940)        merge_semantic_results(
[941](#941)            &mut results,
[942](#942)            manager.search(query, search_fetch_limit(limit, offset))?,
[943](#943)        );
[944](#944)    }
[945](#945)    results.sort_by(|left, right| {
[946](#946)        right
[947](#947)            .score
[948](#948)            .partial_cmp(&left.score)
[949](#949)            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
[950](#950)            .then_with(|| left.path.cmp(&right.path))
[951](#951)    });
[952](#952)    let mut response = paged_bounded_slice_response("results", results, limit, offset)?;
[953](#953)    response["semantic_status"] = json!(status);
[954](#954)    Ok(response)
[955](#955)}
[956](#956)
[957](#957)fn merge_semantic_results(
[958](#958)    results: &mut Vec<open_kioku_core::SearchResult>,
[959](#959)    semantic_results: Vec<open_kioku_core::SearchResult>,
[960](#960)) {
[961](#961)    for semantic in semantic_results {
[962](#962)        if let Some(existing) = results
[963](#963)            .iter_mut()
[964](#964)            .find(|result| result.path == semantic.path)
[965](#965)        {
[966](#966)            for evidence in semantic.evidence {
[967](#967)                if !existing.evidence.contains(&evidence) {
[968](#968)                    existing.evidence.push(evidence);
[969](#969)                }
[970](#970)            }
[971](#971)            for evidence_ref in semantic.evidence_refs {
[972](#972)                if !existing.evidence_refs.contains(&evidence_ref) {
[973](#973)                    existing.evidence_refs.push(evidence_ref);
[974](#974)                }
[975](#975)            }
[976](#976)            for component in semantic.score_breakdown {
[977](#977)                if !existing
[978](#978)                    .score_breakdown
[979](#979)                    .iter()
[980](#980)                    .any(|existing| existing.signal == component.signal)
[981](#981)                {
[982](#982)                    existing.score_breakdown.push(component);
[983](#983)                }
[984](#984)            }
[985](#985)            existing.reconcile_score_breakdown();
[986](#986)        } else {
[987](#987)            results.push(semantic);
[988](#988)        }
[989](#989)    }
[990](#990)}
[991](#991)
[992](#992)fn tool_title(name: &str) -> String {
[993](#993)    let words = name
[994](#994)        .split('_')
[995](#995)        .map(|word| {
[996](#996)            let mut chars = word.chars();
[997](#997)            match chars.next() {
[998](#998)                Some(first) => {
[999](#999)                    first.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() + &chars.as_str().to_lowercase()
[1000](#1000)                }
[1001](#1001)                None => String::new(),
[1002](#1002)            }
[1003](#1003)        })
[1004](#1004)        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
[1005](#1005)        .join(" ");
[1006](#1006)    format!("Open Kioku {words}")
[1007](#1007)}
[1008](#1008)
[1009](#1009)fn tool_annotations(name: &str) -> Value {
[1010](#1010)    let mut read_only = true;
[1011](#1011)    let mut destructive = false;
[1012](#1012)    let mut idempotent = true;
[1013](#1013)    let mut open_world = false;
[1014](#1014)
[1015](#1015)    match name {
[1016](#1016)        "apply_patch" => {
[1017](#1017)            read_only = false;
[1018](#1018)            destructive = true;
[1019](#1019)            idempotent = false;
[1020](#1020)        }
[1021](#1021)        "build_compressed_context"
[1022](#1022)        | "create_change_contract"
[1023](#1023)        | "remember_fact"
[1024](#1024)        | "verify_change_contract" => {
[1025](#1025)            read_only = false;
[1026](#1026)            idempotent = false;
[1027](#1027)        }
[1028](#1028)        "verify_change" => {
[1029](#1029)            read_only = false;
[1030](#1030)            idempotent = false;
[1031](#1031)            open_world = true;
[1032](#1032)        }
[1033](#1033)        _ => {}
[1034](#1034)    }
[1035](#1035)
[1036](#1036)    json!({
[1037](#1037)        "readOnlyHint": read_only,
[1038](#1038)        "destructiveHint": destructive,
[1039](#1039)        "idempotentHint": idempotent,
[1040](#1040)        "openWorldHint": open_world
[1041](#1041)    })
[1042](#1042)}
[1043](#1043)
[1044](#1044)fn tool_output_schema() -> Value {
[1045](#1045)    json!({
[1046](#1046)        "type": "object",
[1047](#1047)        "description": "The MCP structuredContent object returned by this Open Kioku tool. Most tools expose their JSON fields directly; string or scalar tool outputs are wrapped as {\"value\": ...}.",
[1048](#1048)        "additionalProperties": true,
[1049](#1049)        "properties": {
[1050](#1050)            "value": {
[1051](#1051)                "description": "Wrapped non-object output, used for Markdown, TOON, or scalar responses.",
[1052](#1052)            }
[1053](#1053)        }
[1054](#1054)    })
[1055](#1055)}
[1056](#1056)
[1057](#1057)fn tool_description(name: &str, base: &str) -> String {
[1058](#1058)    let guidance = match name {
[1059](#1059)        "repo_status" => "Use first to check whether the local index exists and is fresh enough before calling search, symbol, or graph tools. This is read-only and only inspects repository metadata.",
[1060](#1060)        "list_files" => "Use for broad repository inventory and pagination over indexed paths; use search_files when you already have a keyword or path fragment. This is read-only and returns indexed data only.",
[1061](#1061)        "list_languages" => "Use for a quick language/support overview before choosing language-specific investigation paths. This is read-only and does not rescan the repository.",
[1062](#1062)        "list_symbols" => "Use to browse or substring-filter the symbol table; use search_symbols for fuzzy ranking and get_definition when you need one symbol body. This is read-only.",
[1063](#1063)        "search_symbols" => "Use when an agent has an approximate symbol name and needs ranked candidates; use list_symbols for inventory and get_definition for a resolved definition. This is read-only.",
[1064](#1064)        "detect_architecture" => "Use to infer architectural components from directories when no policy-specific answer is required. Use architecture_policy_check for enforced dependency rules. This is read-only.",
[1065](#1065)        "architecture_boundaries" => "Use to inspect component boundary configuration before explaining or checking violations. Use architecture_violations for legacy detected issues and architecture_policy_check for policy-backed edge evaluation. This is read-only.",
[1066](#1066)        "architecture_violations" => "Use for a quick legacy boundary violation report; use architecture_policy_check when repository policy TOML and indexed dependency edges should be authoritative. This is read-only.",
[1067](#1067)        "architecture_policy_validate" => "Use before architecture_policy_check when editing or debugging policy TOML syntax and component resolution. It validates policy shape only and does not evaluate graph edges.",
[1068](#1068)        "architecture_policy_check" => "Use to enforce architecture policy against indexed import/reference/call edges. Use architecture_policy_validate first for policy syntax errors and architecture_policy_explain for why a specific file or symbol matched. This is read-only.",
[1069](#1069)        "architecture_policy_explain" => "Use after a policy check to explain component membership, public API boundaries, or exemptions for one file, one symbol, or the whole repo. This is read-only and does not change policy.",
[1070](#1070)        "search_code" => "Use for lexical BM25 code search when exact identifiers, terms, routes, or config keys are known. Prefer semantic_search for conceptual queries, hybrid_search when both lexical and semantic evidence are needed, and regex_search for exact patterns. This is read-only.",
[1071](#1071)        "search_files" => "Use when the target is a file path, filename, or file-content keyword rather than a symbol. Prefer list_files for inventory, search_code for code snippets, and regex_search for precise line pattern matching. This is read-only.",
[1072](#1072)        "regex_search" => "Use for exact regular-expression line matches after lexical or semantic search narrows the area. Prefer search_code for ranked keyword search and structural_search for syntax-shaped queries. This is read-only.",
[1073](#1073)        "semantic_status" => "Use before semantic_search or hybrid_search to confirm the local vector index is present and fresh. This is read-only and does not build embeddings.",
[1074](#1074)        "semantic_search" => "Use for natural-language concepts when exact identifiers are unknown. Prefer search_code for exact terms and hybrid_search when results need both semantic recall and lexical precision. This is read-only.",
[1075](#1075)        "hybrid_search" => "Use as the default investigative search when both words and concepts matter. Prefer search_code for deterministic lexical matches and semantic_search for concept-only exploration. This is read-only.",
[1076](#1076)        "explain_search_result" => "Use when a search result must be justified with score components and evidence before relying on it in a plan. Prefer hybrid_search when explanations are unnecessary. This is read-only.",
[1077](#1077)        "structural_search" => "Use for syntax or structure-shaped discovery across symbol trees and chunks. Prefer regex_search for literal text patterns and get_definition for a known symbol. This is read-only.",
[1078](#1078)        "get_definition" => "Use after resolving a symbol name to retrieve its defining range and body. Prefer search_symbols for candidate discovery and get_symbol_context when surrounding references and documentation are needed. This is read-only.",
[1079](#1079)        "get_references" => "Use to find usages of a resolved symbol across the index. Prefer get_callers for caller-only relationships and impact_analysis for broader file-level blast radius. This is read-only.",
[1080](#1080)        "get_implementations" => "Use for traits, interfaces, abstract classes, and protocols where implementation sites matter. Prefer get_references for all usages and get_definition for the declaration itself. This is read-only.",
[1081](#1081)        "get_callers" => "Use to trace inbound calls to a function or method. Prefer get_references for all usages and dependency_path when you need a route between two nodes. This is read-only.",
[1082](#1082)        "get_callees" => "Use to trace outbound calls made by a function or method. Prefer module_dependencies for file/module neighbors and dependency_path for a specific connection. This is read-only.",
[1083](#1083)        "get_symbol_context" => "Use when an agent needs a richer single-symbol bundle than get_definition provides, including file context and docs when indexed. This is read-only.",
[1084](#1084)        "dependency_path" => "Use to explain how two files or symbols are connected through indexed dependencies. Prefer module_dependencies for local neighbors and impact_analysis for downstream blast radius. This is read-only.",
[1085](#1085)        "impact_analysis" => "Use before editing a file to estimate downstream dependents, callers, related tests, and policy impact. Prefer find_tests_for_change when only validation targets are needed. This is read-only.",
[1086](#1086)        "history_provenance_lookup" => "Use when authorship timing or first/last-touch evidence is needed for exactly one path or symbol. Prefer churn_analysis for hotspot metrics and ownership_lookup for maintainers. This is read-only and reports uncertainty.",
[1087](#1087)        "churn_analysis" => "Use to identify hotspots for one path, module, or symbol using materialized git statistics. Prefer history_provenance_lookup for commit provenance and history_similar_changes for prior change examples. This is read-only.",
[1088](#1088)        "history_similar_changes" => "Use during planning to find prior commits related to a task, path, or symbol. Prefer churn_analysis for risk scoring and ownership_lookup for reviewer ownership. This is read-only.",
[1089](#1089)        "ownership_lookup" => "Use to identify likely owners for one path from CODEOWNERS, git history, and memory facts. Prefer reviewer_suggestions when choosing reviewers for a proposed change. This is read-only.",
[1090](#1090)        "reviewer_suggestions" => "Use when a change needs human reviewers and a path is known. Prefer ownership_lookup for ownership evidence without reviewer ranking. This is read-only.",
[1091](#1091)        "module_dependencies" => "Use to inspect direct dependency neighbors for one file or symbol. Prefer dependency_path for a route between two nodes and architecture_policy_check for rule violations. This is read-only.",
[1092](#1092)        "build_context_pack" => "Use before planning or editing to gather relevant files, symbols, tests, history, and policy evidence for a natural-language task. Prefer build_compressed_context when prompt budget is tight. This is read-only.",
[1093](#1093)        "build_compressed_context" => "Use when a context pack is needed but prompt budget is constrained; retrieve_context can expand handles later. This writes reusable context handles under the repository .ok data directory.",
[1094](#1094)        "retrieve_context" => "Use only with handles returned by build_compressed_context to recover original snippets. Prefer build_context_pack for a fresh task-level context bundle. This is read-only.",
[1095](#1095)        "plan_change" => "Use before editing to create an evidence-backed plan with expected files, ranges, impact, and tests. Prefer create_change_contract when the plan must be persisted and verified later. This is read-only.",
[1096](#1096)        "create_change_contract" => "Use when a plan needs a durable verification contract for later review or CI evidence. By default it writes a contract under .ok/contracts; set store=false for a transient contract.",
[1097](#1097)        "get_change_contract" => "Use to retrieve a previously stored contract by id before verification or explanation. Prefer create_change_contract for new contracts. This is read-only.",
[1098](#1098)        "remember_fact" => "Use only for durable, repository-scoped facts an agent should reuse later. It appends memory under repository storage; use search_memory to read existing facts first when unsure.",
[1099](#1099)        "search_memory" => "Use to retrieve stored repository facts by keyword or entity before planning or ownership decisions. Prefer live code/search tools for current source facts. This is read-only.",
[1100](#1100)        "explain_file" => "Use for one known file when parsing status, chunks, and indexed metadata are needed. Prefer search_files to discover files and explain_symbol for symbol-level context. This is read-only.",
[1101](#1101)        "explain_symbol" => "Use for a concise explanation of one known symbol's indexed definition and structure. Prefer get_symbol_context for a larger context bundle. This is read-only.",
[1102](#1102)        "explain_flow" => "Use for a high-level narrative of repository flows and boundaries. Prefer architecture_policy_check for enforceable violations and summarize_architecture for structured architecture output. This is read-only.",
[1103](#1103)        "summarize_architecture" => "Use for a structured architecture overview with layer constraints and violation checks. Prefer explain_flow for a narrative and architecture_policy_explain for file-level evidence. This is read-only.",
[1104](#1104)        "find_tests_for_change" => "Use after identifying a changed file to select relevant test files. Prefer recommend_validation_plan when static checks, coverage, and broader validation steps are also needed. This is read-only.",
[1105](#1105)        "recommend_validation_plan" => "Use before finalizing a change to choose tests, static checks, and coverage actions for one path. Prefer find_tests_for_change for test-only recommendations. This is read-only.",
[1106](#1106)        "explain_test_coverage" => "Use to inspect known coverage evidence for one file or the repository. Prefer recommend_validation_plan when deciding what to run next. This is read-only and does not execute tests.",
[1107](#1107)        "propose_patch" => "Use to draft a patch plan without modifying files. Prefer plan_change for evidence-backed planning and apply_patch only after explicit approval in write-enabled mode. This is read-only.",
[1108](#1108)        "review_patch" => "Use to review a proposed patch plan for safety and completeness before applying it. Prefer validate_patch for boundary/reference validation. This is read-only.",
[1109](#1109)        "validate_patch" => "Use to check a patch plan against architecture boundaries and references before application. Prefer verify_change after a real diff exists. This is read-only.",
[1110](#1110)        "verify_change" => "Use after edits to compare an actual diff or changed files against a saved plan. It may run configured validation commands when run_commands=true and may write attestations when write_attestation=true.",
[1111](#1111)        "verify_change_contract" => "Use after edits to verify a diff against a stored or inline change contract. Stored contract ids append verification records under .ok/contracts, and command execution is opt-in via run_commands.",
[1112](#1112)        "explain_verification" => "Use after verify_change_contract to translate a verification report into a decision, failures, warnings, and next tests. This is read-only.",
[1113](#1113)        "map_stacktrace_to_code" => "Use when runtime stack trace text must be mapped to indexed source locations. Prefer find_errors_for_symbol when the symbol is known and recent stored failures are needed. This tool is read-only and returns disabled status when runtime integration is not configured.",
[1114](#1114)        "find_errors_for_symbol" => "Use to look up recent stored runtime errors for one symbol. Prefer map_stacktrace_to_code for ad hoc stack traces and find_recent_failures for incident inventory. This tool is read-only and returns disabled status when runtime integration is not configured.",
[1115](#1115)        "find_recent_failures" => "Use to list recent stored runtime failures before debugging. Prefer find_errors_for_symbol for a specific symbol. This tool is read-only and returns disabled status when runtime integration is not configured.",
[1116](#1116)        "get_evidence_schema" => "Use before query_evidence_graph to learn available graph node types, edge types, and properties. This is read-only and does not query graph data.",
[1117](#1117)        "query_evidence_graph" => "Use for advanced read-only evidence queries after inspecting get_evidence_schema. The query language is a constrained Cypher-like DSL, not full Cypher; prefer purpose-built tools when available.",
[1118](#1118)        "apply_patch" => "Use only after propose_patch, review_patch, or an equivalent human-approved plan has produced an id and the caller passes approved=true. This mutates the working tree, requires write mode, and should not be used for exploration.",
[1119](#1119)        _ => "Use when this exact indexed repository capability is needed. Prefer narrower sibling tools when they match the task. This tool reports local Open Kioku index data and does not contact external services.",
[1120](#1120)    };
[1121](#1121)
[1122](#1122)    format!("{base} {guidance}")
[1123](#1123)}

[1188](#1188)    let write_tools: &[(&str, &str, Value)] = &[(
[1189](#1189)        "apply_patch",
[1190](#1190)        "Apply an approved patch plan to the codebase. Requires write mode enabled and approval.",
[1191](#1191)        json!({"type":"object","required":["id","approved"],"properties":{"id":{"type":"string","description":"The identifier of the patch plan to apply."},"approved":{"type":"boolean","description":"Must be true to authorize applying the patch."}}}),

[1193](#1193)
[1194](#1194)    let mut tools = Vec::new();
[1195](#1195)    let mut unstable = Vec::new();
[1196](#1196)
[1197](#1197)    for (name, description, schema) in read_only_tools {
[1198](#1198)        let maturity = tool_maturity(name);
[1199](#1199)        if maturity == "experimental" {
[1200](#1200)            unstable.push(name.to_string());
[1201](#1201)            if config.mcp.hide_experimental {
[1202](#1202)                continue;
[1203](#1203)            }
[1204](#1204)        }
[1205](#1205)        tools.push(json!({
[1206](#1206)            "name": name,
[1207](#1207)            "title": tool_title(name),
[1208](#1208)            "description": tool_description(name, description),
[1209](#1209)            "maturity": maturity,
[1210](#1210)            "experimental": maturity == "experimental",
[1211](#1211)            "inputSchema": schema,
[1212](#1212)            "outputSchema": tool_output_schema(),
[1213](#1213)            "annotations": tool_annotations(name)
[1214](#1214)        }));
[1215](#1215)    }
[1216](#1216)
[1217](#1217)    if config.security.allow_write {
[1218](#1218)        for (name, description, schema) in write_tools {
[1219](#1219)            let maturity = tool_maturity(name);
[1220](#1220)            if maturity == "experimental" {
[1221](#1221)                unstable.push(name.to_string());
[1222](#1222)                if config.mcp.hide_experimental {
[1223](#1223)                    continue;
[1224](#1224)                }
[1225](#1225)            }
[1226](#1226)            tools.push(json!({
[1227](#1227)                "name": name,
[1228](#1228)                "title": tool_title(name),
[1229](#1229)                "description": tool_description(name, description),
[1230](#1230)                "maturity": maturity,
[1231](#1231)                "experimental": maturity == "experimental",
[1232](#1232)                "inputSchema": schema,
[1233](#1233)                "outputSchema": tool_output_schema(),
[1234](#1234)                "annotations": tool_annotations(name)
[1235](#1235)            }));
[1236](#1236)        }
[1237](#1237)    }
[1238](#1238)
[1239](#1239)    (tools, unstable)

[1399](#1399)fn graph_query_response(

[1414](#1414)            "arguments": {
[1415](#1415)                "query": query,
[1416](#1416)                "limit": limit,
[1417](#1417)                "offset": next_offset

[1419](#1419)        });
[1420](#1420)    }
[1421](#1421)    Ok(value)

[1424](#1424)fn continuation_handle(method: &str, params: &Value) -> String {
[1425](#1425)    let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();
[1426](#1426)    method.hash(&mut hasher);
[1427](#1427)    serde_json::to_string(params)
[1428](#1428)        .unwrap_or_default()
[1429](#1429)        .hash(&mut hasher);
[1430](#1430)    format!("okc_{:016x}", hasher.finish())
[1431](#1431)}

[1433](#1433)fn continuation_expires_at() -> u64 {
[1434](#1434)    SystemTime::now()
[1435](#1435)        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
[1436](#1436)        .unwrap_or_default()
[1437](#1437)        .as_secs()
[1438](#1438)        .saturating_add(CONTINUATION_TTL_SECS)
[1439](#1439)}
[1440](#1440)
[1441](#1441)fn truncate_utf8(text: &mut String, max_bytes: usize) -> bool {
[1442](#1442)    if text.len() <= max_bytes {
[1443](#1443)        return false;
[1444](#1444)    }
[1445](#1445)    let mut end = max_bytes;
[1446](#1446)    while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
[1447](#1447)        end = end.saturating_sub(1);
[1448](#1448)    }
[1449](#1449)    text.truncate(end);
[1450](#1450)    text.push_str("\n...[truncated]");
[1451](#1451)    true
[1452](#1452)}

[1516](#1516)fn architecture_policy_validate_tool(repo: &Path, params: &Value) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
[1517](#1517)    let (policy, paths) = if let Some(path) = params.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str) {
[1518](#1518)        let path = Path::new(path);
[1519](#1519)        let path = if path.is_absolute() {
[1520](#1520)            path.to_path_buf()
[1521](#1521)        } else {
[1522](#1522)            repo.join(path)
[1523](#1523)        };
[1524](#1524)        (Some(load_architecture_policy_from_path(&path)?), vec![path])
[1525](#1525)    } else {
[1526](#1526)        let policy = load_architecture_policy(repo)?;
[1527](#1527)        let paths = policy
[1528](#1528)            .as_ref()
[1529](#1529)            .map(|policy| policy.source_paths(repo))
[1530](#1530)            .unwrap_or_default();
[1531](#1531)        (policy, paths)
[1532](#1532)    };
[1533](#1533)    let source = policy.as_ref().map(|policy| policy.source);
[1534](#1534)    let configured = policy.is_some();
[1535](#1535)    let message = if let Some(source) = source {
[1536](#1536)        format!("Architecture policy is valid ({source}).")
[1537](#1537)    } else {
[1538](#1538)        "No architecture policy configured. Heuristic architecture detection remains active.".into()
[1539](#1539)    };
[1540](#1540)    Ok(json!({
[1541](#1541)        "valid": true,
[1542](#1542)        "configured": configured,
[1543](#1543)        "source": source,
[1544](#1544)        "paths": paths,
[1545](#1545)        "policy": policy,
[1546](#1546)        "message": message,
[1547](#1547)    }))
[1548](#1548)}
[1549](#1549)
[1550](#1550)fn architecture_policy_explain_tool(
[1551](#1551)    repo: &Path,
[1552](#1552)    store: &SqliteStore,
[1553](#1553)    resolver: &PolicyResolver,
[1554](#1554)    policy: &open_kioku_config::ArchitecturePolicy,
[1555](#1555)    params: &Value,
[1556](#1556)) -> anyhow::Result<Value> {
[1557](#1557)    let file = params.get("file").and_then(Value::as_str);
[1558](#1558)    let symbol = params.get("symbol").and_then(Value::as_str);
[1559](#1559)    let scope = params.get("scope").and_then(Value::as_str);
[1560](#1560)    if let Some(scope) = scope {
[1561](#1561)        anyhow::ensure!(
[1562](#1562)            scope == "repo",
[1563](#1563)            "unsupported architecture policy scope `{scope}`"
[1564](#1564)        );
[1565](#1565)    }
[1566](#1566)    let selectors = file.is_some() as u8 + symbol.is_some() as u8 + scope.is_some() as u8;
[1567](#1567)    anyhow::ensure!(
[1568](#1568)        selectors <= 1,
[1569](#1569)        "provide exactly one of `file`, `symbol`, or `scope`"
[1570](#1570)    );
[1571](#1571)    let (query_kind, query, file_path, symbol_value) = match (file, symbol, scope) {
[1572](#1572)        (Some(path), None, None) => {
[1573](#1573)            let path = repo_relative_path(repo, Path::new(path));
[1574](#1574)            ("file", path.display().to_string(), Some(path), Value::Null)
[1575](#1575)        }
[1576](#1576)        (None, Some(query), None) => {
[1577](#1577)            let symbol = SymbolEngine::new(store).definition(query)?;
[1578](#1578)            let file_path = file_path_for_symbol(store, &symbol)?;
[1579](#1579)            (
[1580](#1580)                "symbol",
[1581](#1581)                query.to_string(),
[1582](#1582)                Some(file_path),
[1583](#1583)                serde_json::to_value(symbol)?,
[1584](#1584)            )
[1585](#1585)        }
[1586](#1586)        (None, None, Some("repo")) | (None, None, None) => {
[1587](#1587)            ("repo", repo.display().to_string(), None, Value::Null)
[1588](#1588)        }
[1589](#1589)        _ => unreachable!("selector count was validated above"),
[1590](#1590)    };
[1591](#1591)    let mut uncertainty = Vec::new();
[1592](#1592)    let components = if let Some(file_path) = &file_path {
[1593](#1593)        match resolver.resolve_node(file_path, None) {
[1594](#1594)            Ok(resolved) => resolved.components,
[1595](#1595)            Err(unmapped) => {
[1596](#1596)                uncertainty.push(format!(
[1597](#1597)                    "{} did not match any architecture policy component",
[1598](#1598)                    unmapped.file_path.display()
[1599](#1599)                ));
[1600](#1600)                Vec::new()
[1601](#1601)            }
[1602](#1602)        }
[1603](#1603)    } else {
[1604](#1604)        Vec::new()
[1605](#1605)    };
[1606](#1606)    let boundary = evaluate_public_api_boundary(store, resolver, policy)?;
[1607](#1607)    let violations = boundary
[1608](#1608)        .violations
[1609](#1609)        .into_iter()
[1610](#1610)        .filter(|violation| match &file_path {
[1611](#1611)            Some(file_path) => {
[1612](#1612)                violation.source_path == *file_path || violation.target_path == *file_path
[1613](#1613)            }
[1614](#1614)            None => true,
[1615](#1615)        })
[1616](#1616)        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[1617](#1617)    let exemptions = boundary
[1618](#1618)        .exemptions
[1619](#1619)        .into_iter()
[1620](#1620)        .filter(|exemption| match &file_path {
[1621](#1621)            Some(file_path) => {
[1622](#1622)                exemption.source_path == *file_path || exemption.target_path == *file_path
[1623](#1623)            }
[1624](#1624)            None => true,
[1625](#1625)        })
[1626](#1626)        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[1627](#1627)    uncertainty.extend(boundary.uncertainty);
[1628](#1628)    if file_path.is_some() && violations.is_empty() && exemptions.is_empty() {
[1629](#1629)        uncertainty.push("no public API boundary findings matched this query".into());
[1630](#1630)    }
[1631](#1631)    uncertainty.sort();
[1632](#1632)    uncertainty.dedup();
[1633](#1633)    Ok(json!({
[1634](#1634)        "configured": true,
[1635](#1635)        "query_kind": query_kind,
[1636](#1636)        "query": query,
[1637](#1637)        "file_path": file_path,
[1638](#1638)        "symbol": symbol_value,
[1639](#1639)        "components": components,
[1640](#1640)        "violations": violations,
[1641](#1641)        "exemptions": exemptions,
[1642](#1642)        "uncertainty": uncertainty,
[1643](#1643)        "message": format!(
[1644](#1644)            "Architecture policy explanation for {query_kind} `{query}`: {} component match(es), {} violation(s), {} exemption(s).",
[1645](#1645)            components.len(),
[1646](#1646)            violations.len(),
[1647](#1647)            exemptions.len()
[1648](#1648)        )
[1649](#1649)    }))
[1650](#1650)}
[1651](#1651)
[1652](#1652)fn file_path_for_symbol(
[1653](#1653)    store: &dyn MetadataStore,
[1654](#1654)    symbol: &open_kioku_core::Symbol,
[1655](#1655)) -> anyhow::Result<PathBuf> {
[1656](#1656)    let files = store.list_files(usize::MAX, 0)?;
[1657](#1657)    files
[1658](#1658)        .into_iter()
[1659](#1659)        .find(|file| file.id == symbol.file_id)
[1660](#1660)        .map(|file| file.path)
[1661](#1661)        .with_context(|| {
[1662](#1662)            format!(
[1663](#1663)                "indexed symbol `{}` references missing file id `{}`",
[1664](#1664)                symbol.qualified_name, symbol.file_id.0
[1665](#1665)            )
[1666](#1666)        })
[1667](#1667)}
[1668](#1668)
[1669](#1669)fn repo_relative_path(repo: &Path, path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
[1670](#1670)    if path.is_absolute() {
[1671](#1671)        path.strip_prefix(repo).unwrap_or(path).to_path_buf()
[1672](#1672)    } else {
[1673](#1673)        path.to_path_buf()
[1674](#1674)    }
[1675](#1675)}
[1676](#1676)
[1677](#1677)fn similar_change_query_from_params(params: &Value) -> anyhow::Result<SimilarChangeQuery> {
[1678](#1678)    let task = params
[1679](#1679)        .get("task")
[1680](#1680)        .and_then(Value::as_str)
[1681](#1681)        .map(str::trim)
[1682](#1682)        .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
[1683](#1683)        .map(str::to_string);
[1684](#1684)    let mut paths = Vec::new();
[1685](#1685)    if let Some(path) = params.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str) {
[1686](#1686)        paths.push(PathBuf::from(path));
[1687](#1687)    }
[1688](#1688)    if let Some(values) = params.get("paths").and_then(Value::as_array) {
[1689](#1689)        for value in values {
[1690](#1690)            let Some(path) = value.as_str() else {
[1691](#1691)                anyhow::bail!("`paths` must contain only strings");
[1692](#1692)            };
[1693](#1693)            paths.push(PathBuf::from(path));
[1694](#1694)        }
[1695](#1695)    }
[1696](#1696)    let mut symbols = Vec::new();
[1697](#1697)    if let Some(symbol) = params.get("symbol").and_then(Value::as_str) {
[1698](#1698)        symbols.push(symbol.to_string());
[1699](#1699)    }
[1700](#1700)    if let Some(values) = params.get("symbols").and_then(Value::as_array) {
[1701](#1701)        for value in values {
[1702](#1702)            let Some(symbol) = value.as_str() else {
[1703](#1703)                anyhow::bail!("`symbols` must contain only strings");
[1704](#1704)            };
[1705](#1705)            symbols.push(symbol.to_string());
[1706](#1706)        }
[1707](#1707)    }
[1708](#1708)    if task.is_none() && paths.is_empty() && symbols.is_empty() {
[1709](#1709)        anyhow::bail!("provide at least one of `task`, `path`/`paths`, or `symbol`/`symbols`");
[1710](#1710)    }
[1711](#1711)    Ok(SimilarChangeQuery {
[1712](#1712)        task,
[1713](#1713)        paths,
[1714](#1714)        symbols,
[1715](#1715)    })
[1716](#1716)}
[1717](#1717)
[1718](#1718)fn required_str<'a>(params: &'a Value, key: &str) -> anyhow::Result<&'a str> {
[1719](#1719)    params
[1720](#1720)        .get(key)
[1721](#1721)        .and_then(Value::as_str)
[1722](#1722)        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("missing required string argument `{key}`"))
[1723](#1723)}
[1724](#1724)
[1725](#1725)fn changed_ranges_since(repo: &Path, since: &str) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<open_kioku_git::DiffFile>> {
[1726](#1726)    Ok(open_kioku_git::diff_unified_zero_since(repo, since)?)
[1727](#1727)}
[1728](#1728)
[1729](#1729)fn task_with_changed_ranges(repo: &Path, task: &str, since: &str) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
[1730](#1730)    let changed = changed_ranges_since(repo, since)?;
[1731](#1731)    if changed.is_empty() {
[1732](#1732)        return Ok(format!(
[1733](#1733)            "{task}\n\nGit diff since `{since}` has no changed files."
[1734](#1734)        ));
[1735](#1735)    }
[1736](#1736)    let mut enriched =
[1737](#1737)        format!("{task}\n\nChanged files and line ranges from `git diff {since} --unified=0`:\n");
[1738](#1738)    for change in &changed {
[1739](#1739)        enriched.push_str("- ");
[1740](#1740)        enriched.push_str(&render_changed_range(change));
[1741](#1741)        enriched.push('\n');
[1742](#1742)    }
[1743](#1743)    Ok(enriched)
[1744](#1744)}
[1745](#1745)
[1746](#1746)fn render_changed_range(change: &open_kioku_git::DiffFile) -> String {
[1747](#1747)    let path = change
[1748](#1748)        .new_path
[1749](#1749)        .as_ref()
[1750](#1750)        .or(change.old_path.as_ref())
[1751](#1751)        .map(|path| path.display().to_string())
[1752](#1752)        .unwrap_or_else(|| "<unknown>".into());
[1753](#1753)    let ranges = change
[1754](#1754)        .hunks
[1755](#1755)        .iter()
[1756](#1756)        .filter_map(|hunk| hunk.new_range.as_ref().or(hunk.old_range.as_ref()))
[1757](#1757)        .map(|range| {
[1758](#1758)            if range.start == range.end {
[1759](#1759)                range.start.to_string()
[1760](#1760)            } else {
[1761](#1761)                format!("{}-{}", range.start, range.end)
[1762](#1762)            }
[1763](#1763)        })
[1764](#1764)        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
[1765](#1765)    if ranges.is_empty() {
[1766](#1766)        format!("{:?} {}", change.status, path)
[1767](#1767)    } else {
[1768](#1768)        format!("{:?} {} lines {}", change.status, path, ranges.join(","))
[1769](#1769)    }
[1770](#1770)}
[1771](#1771)
[1772](#1772)fn git_diff_since(repo: &Path, since: &str) -> anyhow::Result<Option<String>> {
[1773](#1773)    let output = std::process::Command::new("git")
[1774](#1774)        .arg("-C")
[1775](#1775)        .arg(repo)
[1776](#1776)        .args(["diff", "--unified=0", "--no-ext-diff", "--relative"])
[1777](#1777)        .arg(since)
[1778](#1778)        .output()?;
[1779](#1779)    if !output.status.success() {
[1780](#1780)        anyhow::bail!(
[1781](#1781)            "git diff failed: {}",
[1782](#1782)            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
[1783](#1783)        );
[1784](#1784)    }
[1785](#1785)    Ok(Some(String::from_utf8(output.stdout)?))
[1786](#1786)}
